subject: EdgeAI discovery: burst latency, streaming UX & concurrency — summary and next steps
messages:
From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@edgeai.io>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: EdgeAI discovery: burst latency, streaming UX & concurrency — summary and next steps

Alex — thanks again for the 30-min sync this morning. Quick write-up to capture what we heard and make sure we’re aligned on next steps. Please correct anything I’ve missed.

Key pain points you shared
- Intermittent burst latency during live streaming sessions (p95 spikes up to ~1.9s) causing UX stutters.
- High tail latency during peak concurrency; current infra struggles when >120 simultaneous streams are active.
- Existing batching approach reduces cost but increases jitter for streaming clients.

Current stack we discussed
- On-prem GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100-ish), custom inference layer, Triton in some workloads.
- Model family: Llama2-13B (custom fine-tuned), average request length ~512 tokens, peaks ~2k.
- Traffic pattern: 40% low-latency streaming (real-time chat/audio transcripts), 60% batch/async.

Success criteria you called out
- p95 streaming latency <500ms end-to-end (in-app perceived latency).
- Consistent p99 <1s during sustained peaks.
- Support 150+ concurrent streaming sessions without >10% request drop or timeouts.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Rishi to run a focused perf plan: lightweight perf test (1–2 models, representative seq lengths) vs. your traces. Expected duration 1 week. Attachment: redwood-sizing-estimate.csv (draft).
2) You to share a redacted trace bundle (we discussed edgeai-traces.zip).
3) Align on an SLA baseline and potential dedicated pool sizing — Marcus will draft an initial cost/throughput estimate.
4) Quick follow-up technical call to review perf results and sizing (30 min) — propose Wed 13 Jan or Thu 14 Jan.

Attachments: edgeai-traces.zip (placeholder), redwood-sizing-estimate.csv (placeholder)

Thanks — ping me if any item above needs correction.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@edgeai.io>

Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EdgeAI discovery: burst latency, streaming UX & concurrency — summary and next steps

Thanks Jasmine — that captures it well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 1.9s p95 was measured client-side during a recent load test where we saw a burst from 80 -> 180 simultaneous streams over ~30s. Baseline p95 is ~420ms outside of bursts.
- Our current Triton setup batches aggressively for throughput; streaming requests are handled by a separate microservice but still hit the same GPU pool under contention.
- Model details: Llama2-13B finetuned on internal corpus. Quantization hasn’t been pushed to prod yet.
- Sequence distribution: median ~512, 95th ~1024, peaks at ~2048 for long transcripts.

We’ll share a sanitized traces bundle by EOD Monday — it will include sample request logs and a small set of raw spans (no PII).

On the perf test: we’re happy to run with a single model initially. Wed 13 Jan works for a 30-min technical review for our SRE and model infra lead.

Attachment: sample_client_trace.json (in traces bundle)

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering | EdgeAI
alex.johnson@edgeai.io
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: alex.johnson@edgeai.io, jasmine.liu@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EdgeAI discovery: burst latency, streaming UX & concurrency — summary and next steps

Alex / team — quick technical follow-up after reading the notes and previewing the traces you mentioned. I want to make sure the perf run targets the right scenarios.

Questions / assumptions
1) Are streaming sessions long-lived (minutes) or short-lived (tens of seconds)? That changes KV-cache behavior.
2) Do you need token-by-token streaming (low latency per token) or chunked frames (e.g., ~200 ms windows)?
3) Is it acceptable to use a quantized model variant in service of lower latency if quality impact is <5%?

Outline of our proposed perf plan
- Step A: Replay your traces against a mirror of your model (or our closest match) with: (a) token streaming enabled, (b) KV caching warmup, (c) burst scenarios (ramp to 180 streams in 30s).
- Step B: Compare three runtime configs: baseline (your current), Redwood continuous-batching optimized for streaming, and a dedicated streaming pool with pre-warmed KV cache.
- Step C: Produce a small report with p50/p95/p99, tail jitter graphs, and recommended pool sizes.

Initial sizing (thin estimate) — very approximate
- For Llama2-13B, avg seq 512, target 150 concurrent streams with streaming token cadence: ~6–8 GPUs in a dedicated streaming pool (depends on quantization and token cadence).

I attached a draft sizing worksheet (redwood-sizing-estimate.csv) — contains the assumptions above. If the sequence cadence is token-by-token, we may need more aggressive pre-warm and smaller batching.

Next step: once we have traces, we’ll run the replay and share results. Planning note: perf run (single model) ~3–4 days including validation and checks if we queue it this week.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@edgeai.io>

Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 12:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EdgeAI discovery: burst latency, streaming UX & concurrency — summary and next steps

Rishi — answers inline below.

> 1) Are streaming sessions long-lived (minutes) or short-lived (tens of seconds)?
Mostly short-lived sessions (30–90s), but we have a subset of streaming workflows ~5–10 minutes (human-in-the-loop sessions).

> 2) Do you need token-by-token streaming or chunked frames?
Token-by-token preferred for conversational UX, but chunked frames (200–300ms) are acceptable as a fallback if it materially reduces tail latency.

> 3) Is quantized model acceptable?
We can trial a quantized variant in staging; quality regression needs to be <3% on our evaluation set.

We’ll upload the sanitized traces to the secure S3 link Jasmine requested by EOD Monday. Also including a small PDF with our current SLAs and uptime constraints.

We’re good to aim for Wed 13 Jan for the technical review — I’ll have our SRE lead join.

— Alex
